ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit in the figure has four main nodes: the middle-left node can be labeled L, the middle node can be labeled C, the middle-right node can be labeled R, and the bottom common node can be labeled B. It can be seen that R1 connects L and C, R2 connects C and R, and R3 vertically connects C and B; the left current source Is connects L and B; in the right branch, R5 and the voltage source Us are in series, and as a whole connect R and B; the top resistor R4 connects L and R. Reasoning: After abstracting according to these main nodes into a node graph, among the four nodes L, C, R, and B, there is a branch connected between any two points, so this graph is equivalent to the complete graph K4. The number of simple three-node loops in K4 is C(4,3)=4; the number of four-node loops is 3. The total number of loops is 4+3=7.

raw_record.question_text: How many loops are in the circuit shown in the figure?

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit as a node graph from the image. Label the left junction L, center junction C, right junction R, and bottom junction B. Note that every pair of these four nodes is connected by a branch: L-C through R1, C-R through R2, C-B through R3, L-B through the current source, R-B through R5 and Us in series, and L-R through R4. Since these connections form K4, count all simple cycles: there are C(4,3)=4 three-node loops and 3 four-node loops. Add them to get 7 loops.
